title: Finite and common-stage point realization composites and scalar component
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its finite coefficient stages and inclusions [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Use the actual finite and common-stage point fibre functors [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Define the finite point realization to be $\operatorname{pointRationalFibre}\mathbin{\ggg}\iota$, where $\iota$ is the full inclusion of bounded finite-dimensional complexes into $D(E)$ [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. Define the common-stage point realization to be $\operatorname{pointQbarFibre}\mathbin{\ggg}\operatorname{pointFdQbarRealization}$ [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. For a finite stage $E$, define its coefficient-model map by the canonical Shrink algebra equivalence to the actual subfield of $\Omega$. Define the common-stage object isomorphism using the specified object formula of $\operatorname{pointQbarFibre}$ on the actual stage inclusion: its realization is the successive derived scalar extension from the coefficient model to $E$ and then to $\Omega$. Define the canonical finite-to-common scalar component as the inverse of the normalized derived tensor-tower component [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower], followed by the inverse of this common-stage object isomorphism. Its source is direct derived scalar extension of the finite point realization to $\Omega$ and its target is the actual common-stage point realization of that same included object. These constructions introduce no arbitrary comparison isomorphism and assert no t-exactness theorem.
